name: what a crowd costs to draw

steps.note: frames, not ticks: the sim on its fixed step, the sprite sync, the UI and the render
sprites are culled to the canvas, so what is drawn is a fact about the view
and not about the crowd - the claims below are phrased accordingly
paused first, so the crowd cannot wander between a step and the step after it
an empty map first - the map's own tiles, the HUD and the pipeline
200 actors, spread over a 48x32 plaza; the canvas shows about 7x4 cells of it
a thousand: far more than fit on the canvas, and only the ones on it are drawn
dogs draw from an atlas and step their animation every frame

steps.shot: a thousand actors and five hundred dogs

steps.note: 1500 units and a 48x32 map, and the world holds a couple of hundred sprites:
the tiles under the canvas, the few dozen units standing on them, their
overlays, and the sprites parked for reuse. Everything here is a function of
the canvas. Unculled this was 1536 tiles plus some 6000 sprites of crowd.
It is also the only assertion that notices a pool growing with the crowd:
a parked body carries no Actor, so expect_sprites cannot see one.
the frame cost per actor must not grow as the crowd does. Culling makes this
a demand for sublinearity rather than for flatness: five times the crowd
draws the same few dozen sprites, so the cost per entity should fall.
and a wall, set well above what this machine does - see qa-perf/ for the number
zooming in rebuilds the canvas smaller, so it shows less world and draws less:
the same assertions hold, against a view that has changed underneath them
and leaving takes every one of those sprites away, parked ones included
